claims.text: An ultra-thin conformal Al2O3 coating can be deposited on boride-based components by atomic layer deposition.
The ALD Al2O3 coating will significantly improve the molten-aluminum corrosion resistance of boride-based components.
The coating improves corrosion resistance by inhibiting direct chemical interactions at the molten-aluminum/boride interface.
The coating improves corrosion resistance by inhibiting galvanic interactions at the interface.
TiB2 is an example of a conventional boride-based component material used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment.
A 50–100 nm Al2O3 barrier coating is an appropriate thickness range for the proposed intervention.
The proposed Al2O3 coating can be deposited by ALD at temperatures no higher than 250°C.
Post-deposition annealing may enhance the thermal stability or adhesion of the Al2O3 coating.
Approximately 700°C represents typical molten-aluminum exposure conditions for hot-dip aluminum plating.
ALD will produce a continuous, dense, nanometer-thick alumina layer on the boride surface.
The alumina layer will act as an inert diffusion barrier against molten aluminum.
The alumina layer will prevent direct contact between molten aluminum and the boride substrate.
Preventing direct contact will reduce reactive and galvanic corrosion processes.
Relative to uncoated controls, coated components will show a marked decrease in corrosion penetration.
Relative to uncoated controls, coated components will have enhanced durability during prolonged molten-aluminum exposure.
Protection will persist only while coating adhesion and continuity are maintained during high-temperature exposure and thermal cycling.
Cracking or delamination of the coating will nullify its protective effect.
